slug: 2026-06-23 Implications of Zimbabwe’s National AI Strategy on Freedom of Expression Privacy and Access to Information

facts.fact: MISA Zimbabwe, a media-freedom body inside the country, published an analysis criticising the Zimbabwe National AI Strategy 2026-2030, including its proposed National Reality Check Platform for truth-verification, as lacking legal safeguards for freedom of expression.

facts.fact: CIPESA says an internet shutdown was ordered in Zimbabwe in January 2019 amid nationwide fuel-price protests, by the state security minister through an intercept directive to mobile network operators, and was later restored; end date not given.

CIPESA says Zimbabwe's High Court ruled in January 2019 that the state security minister had no authority under the Interception of Communications Act to order an internet shutdown or issue an intercept directive to mobile network operators.
facts.system: High Court ruling on the 2019 internet shutdown

note: Mozambique, Togo, Nigeria, Guinea and Senegal items are other countries and give no ZWE fact.
Says only that Zimbabwe has experienced internet disruptions and platform restrictions, with no date, event or orderer; the Zambia items are not ZWE.

facts.fact: CIPESA says Zimbabwe experienced network degradation during its 2023 elections; the document does not say who ordered it, where, or when it ended.

systems.system: Offences of false information, cyberbullying, incitement, insulting the President, sovereignty and national interest

note: Says journalists and critics in Zimbabwe face arrest generally, with no person, date or case named, so no penalty fact; the Uganda shutdown is not ZWE. The UPR submission by ZLHR and partners is itself civil-society criticism but of no named policy, bill or decision.

Excerpt only: names 'election-period network disruptions' without saying who ordered them, what was cut or when; the 2023 slowdown appears only as a footnote title; recommendations to repeal speech offences and end arrests give no dated event or named person, so no fact.
An access-to-information law (other); it repeals the Access to Information and Protection of Privacy Act but not a speech offence, so no fact.

systems.system: Cyber and Data Protection Act [Chapter 12:07] (No. 5 of 2021), s.164C false data message offence
systems.owner: Parliament of Zimbabwe; POTRAZ designated Data Protection Authority

note: A speech law (s.164C, false data message, up to five years) gazetted 11 March 2022 with no one reported charged; the document is statute text and states no cut, punishment or repeal, so no fact.

facts.fact: The Media Alliance of Zimbabwe, with International Media Support, held a dialogue criticising the Cyber and Data Protection Act as being used to silence journalists.
MAZ's coordinator says four journalists were reportedly arrested in 2026 on cyberbullying charges over stories they wrote.

Amnesty International says Bulawayo24 journalist Gideon Madzikatidze has been in custody since 18 February 2026, charged with cyberbullying and broadcasting without a licence, after publishing a story alleging corruption involving a waste management company.
The Southern Africa Litigation Centre says courts in Zimbabwe struck down criminal defamation, giving no date.

note: No date for the ruling; as_of is the document's date.
Only a press-freedom ranking and an unspecific decline in violations; no dated criticism, punishment, cut or repeal.
Document states nothing this study asks for this country.

facts.fact: ICT Minister Tatenda Mavetera says government is applying legal frameworks to arrest people spreading misinformation, disinformation and fake news; police report several convictions for false transmission of messages.

Paradigm Initiative's Londa 2025 report states that in 2025 arbitrary arrests of journalists and human rights defenders continued in Zimbabwe and that sedition legislation and the criminalisation of false news were applied against freedom of expression.

note: Report also says there was no internet shutdown in 2025; that is not a cut or a bar, so no fact.
The document is about the continental MIL framework; it states nothing on this study for Zimbabwe.
Netherlands-funded CRS grant for advocacy toward an AI legal framework and policy brief; planned deliverables only, nothing delivered or adopted stated.
No criticism, cut or punishment stated.

facts.fact: CPJ reports that Bulawayo24 reporter Gideon Madzikatidze has been detained since 18 February 2026 on charges of cyberbullying and broadcasting without a licence over a December 2025 web story alleging that a local waste company bribed journalists.
GroundUp says Zimbabwe Independent editor Faith Zaba was arrested in July 2025 on insult charges over a satirical column on President Mnangagwa and held three nights.
GroundUp says HSTV head Blessed Mhlanga spent 72 days in pretrial detention in 2025 after interviewing a war veteran who accused the president of corruption.

Freedom House says journalist Blessed Mhlanga was arrested and charged with inciting violence in February 2025 over an interview calling for the president's resignation, and was held nearly three months.
Global Voices says Zimbabwe's January 2019 shutdown directives were set aside by the High Court on the ground that the minister lacked power to issue them.

note: No named in-country group criticising a named policy, no cut or punishment stated; the analysis is by a regional body.
